title: BlackRock Files for Two New Tokenized Funds as Wall Street's Blockchain Push Accelerates
excerpt: The world's largest asset manager is expanding its onchain lineup with a stablecoin reserve vehicle and a tokenized share class for a $6.1 billion money-market fund, building on the success of its BUIDL fund that has crossed $2.5 billion in assets.
body:
• BlackRock filed two SEC applications to expand its tokenized fund lineup: a new stablecoin reserve vehicle requiring a $3 million minimum investment, and a tokenized share class for its $6.1 billion Select Treasury Based Liquidity Fund on Ethereum.
  • The filings build on BlackRock's BUIDL fund, which launched in March 2024 and now manages over $2.5 billion across eight blockchains including Ethereum, Solana, and Aptos, with $100 million in cumulative payouts to investors.
  • The tokenized U.S. Treasury market has grown rapidly, with BUIDL holding a 34 per cent market share, and J.P. Morgan analysts suggesting tokenized money market funds could compete directly with stablecoins.
  • The moves signal that traditional finance's embrace of blockchain infrastructure is moving from experimentation to institutional scale.

From Experiment to Product Line

BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager with $14 trillion under management, is no longer dabbling in blockchain-based finance. The firm filed two applications with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in May to expand its tokenized fund offerings, turning what began as a single experimental product into a growing product line aimed squarely at capturing capital sitting idle in stablecoins.

The first filing proposes a BlackRock Daily Reinvestment Stablecoin Reserve Vehicle — a fund that would invest in cash, short-term U.S. Treasuries with maturities of 93 days or less, and overnight repurchase agreements backed by Treasuries. The fund would issue "OnChain Shares" through a permissioned framework connected to multiple public blockchains, with Securitize Transfer Agent LLC as the transfer agent. Entry requires a $3 million minimum investment, restricting access to institutional buyers.

The second filing tokenizes an existing product: the BlackRock Select Treasury Based Liquidity Fund, a roughly $6.1 billion money-market vehicle. The new share class would trade on Ethereum alongside the fund's traditional shares, with BNY Mellon Investment Servicing maintaining shareholder records using the ERC-20 token standard.

BUIDL's Track Record

Both filings build on the success of BUIDL — the BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund — which launched in March 2024 on Ethereum and has since expanded to eight blockchains including Solana, Aptos, Avalanche, Arbitrum, and Optimism.

The fund has crossed $2.5 billion in assets under management and delivered $100 million in cumulative payouts to investors, a milestone announced by Securitize that demonstrates blockchain-based finance operating at institutional scale. BUIDL holds a 34 per cent share of the tokenized U.S. Treasury market, according to RWA.xyz data.

"In the year since BUIDL's launch, we've experienced significant growth in demand for tokenized real-world assets, reinforcing the value of bringing institutional-grade products on-chain."

— Carlos Domingo, Co-founder and CEO, Securitize

Competing With Stablecoins

The strategic logic behind BlackRock's expansion is straightforward: billions of dollars sit in stablecoins that earn no yield for their holders. Tokenized money market funds offer the same blockchain-native liquidity and 24/7 access, but with the added benefit of Treasury-backed returns.

J.P. Morgan analyst Teresa Ho suggested in July that tokenized money market funds could compete directly with stablecoins by preserving cash-like characteristics while generating yield. The comment came as regulatory frameworks like the GENIUS Act advanced stablecoin adoption in parallel.

BlackRock isn't alone in the space. Franklin Templeton operates a competing tokenized fund with a $692 million market capitalisation. Other significant players include Hashnote's Short Duration Yield Coin and Ondo's U.S. Dollar Yield product.

What Indian Investors Should Watch

For Indian investors and the diaspora with exposure to global markets, BlackRock's push into tokenized finance signals a broader institutional validation of blockchain infrastructure. India's own regulatory stance on crypto and tokenized assets remains cautious, but the participation of the world's largest asset manager in this space — alongside established custodians like BNY Mellon — suggests the technology is moving from the periphery to the mainstream of global finance. The implications for cross-border remittances, settlement efficiency, and access to dollar-denominated yields are particularly relevant for NRI investors managing assets across jurisdictions.
